title: Assistant-first opening

assessment.title: Synthetic measurement evidence assessment
assessment.learning_objective: Explain how reliability, measurement error, and validity evidence support different claims about scores.
assessment.assessment_boundary: Only the three administered measurement-theory items and directly related concepts may be discussed.

administered_items.item_stem: A test has a high internal-consistency coefficient. Which conclusion is best supported?

options.label: A
options.text: The scores are internally consistent, but validity still needs separate evidence.

options.label: B
options.text: The high coefficient proves the scores are valid for every intended use.

options.label: C
options.text: The coefficient proves every observed score is free from measurement error.

administered_items.answer_explanation: Internal consistency concerns how coherently scores behave. It does not by itself establish evidence for a particular interpretation or use.

distractor_rationales.B: Conflates reliability evidence with validity evidence.
distractor_rationales.C: Treats a group-level reliability coefficient as error-free individual measurement.

expected_reasoning_patterns: Distinguishes score consistency from evidence for an intended interpretation.

administered_items.item_stem: What does the standard error of measurement contribute when interpreting an observed score?

options.label: A
options.text: It describes expected measurement error around an observed score.

options.label: B
options.text: It proves the observed score is the person's exact true score.

options.label: C
options.text: It reports the percentage of items answered incorrectly.

administered_items.answer_explanation: The standard error of measurement represents expected score uncertainty; it does not make an observed score exact.

distractor_rationales.B: Removes uncertainty rather than representing it.
distractor_rationales.C: Confuses measurement error with an item-level error percentage.

expected_reasoning_patterns: Connects the standard error of measurement with uncertainty around observed scores.

administered_items.item_stem: Which statement best reflects a contemporary validity argument?

options.label: A
options.text: Evidence is evaluated for the intended interpretation and use of scores.

options.label: B
options.text: Validity is automatically established whenever reliability is high.

options.label: C
options.text: Validity is a permanent property of the test independent of context.

administered_items.answer_explanation: Validity concerns the evidence supporting an intended score interpretation and use in context, not a context-free property of a test.

distractor_rationales.B: Treats reliability as sufficient validity evidence.
distractor_rationales.C: Treats validity as detached from interpretation, use, and context.

expected_reasoning_patterns: Relates validity evidence to an intended interpretation and use.

assessment_responses.tempting_option_reason: The coefficient sounded like broad evidence that the test works.
assessment_responses.reasoning_text: A high coefficient supports consistency, but validity is a different question.

assessment_responses.tempting_option_reason: An exact true score sounded simpler than an uncertainty statement.
assessment_responses.reasoning_text: SEM tells us there is error around an observed score.

assessment_responses.tempting_option_reason: I used to think validity belonged to the test itself.
assessment_responses.reasoning_text: Validity evidence should fit the intended use.
